# `test/vendor/yapr/` — the second reader

GENERATED by yapr's `build.sh`. Do not edit a file here; rebuild yapr and copy `dist/yapr_wasm.js` and `dist/yapr_wasm_bg.wasm` over these, then update the commit below.

[yapr](https://gitlab.com/aicof-design-team/yapr) is a PDF viewer whose engine is hayro, a pure-Rust PDF renderer, in PdfCraft's hardened copies, compiled to WebAssembly (MIT OR Apache-2.0). `test/read-back-yapr.ts` loads it in node, and `scripts/compare.ts` asks it where a written file put its glyphs and what its pages look like, the questions mupdf is asked, so that two readers written by different people answer them independently (*a second reader is asked the same question*, DESIGN.md S83). Nothing here ships: the module is read by the gate of the Rust writer alone (`npm run identity -- compare`), never by `npm test`, which is why it lives under `test/` and not beside the committed bundles in `vendor/`. Copied from the BelType monorepo's `packages/caster/test/vendor/yapr/` on 2026-11-03, unchanged but this paragraph.

| file | bytes | what it is |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `yapr_wasm.js` | 11725 | wasm-bindgen's glue for the `web` target; `default()` takes `{ module_or_path }`, which node hands the bytes |
| `yapr_wasm_bg.wasm` | 4328659 | the module, unoptimised by `wasm-opt -Oz`; 1.5 MB under Brotli, which the suite never needs |

**Source:** yapr commit `9d0144a` (2026-10-19), the one that added `Viewer.text(page)` for this reader, built with rustc 1.99.1, wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 and binaryen 133.
